\begin{frame}{Graph Laplacian and Quadratic Forms}
  \framesubtitle{Discrete Potential Theory}
  Let $G = (V, E)$ be an undirected, weighted graph with adjacency matrix $W$.
  The combinatorial Laplacian $L$ is defined as:
  \begin{equation}
    L = D - W, \quad D_{ii} = \sum_{j \in V} W_{ij}
  \end{equation}

  \pause
  For any real-valued potential vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^{|V|}$:
  \begin{equation}
    x^T L x = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i,j \in V} W_{ij} (x_i - x_j)^2 \ge 0
  \end{equation}
  \pause
  Hence $L$ is positive semidefinite ($L \succeq 0$) with trivial kernel $\mathbf{1} \in \ker(L)$.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Cheeger Inequality and Conductance}
  \begin{theorem}[Cheeger's Discrete Inequality]
    Let $\lambda_2$ be the algebraic connectivity of $G$. The graph conductance $h(G)$ satisfies:
    \begin{equation*}
      \frac{\lambda_2}{2} \le h(G) \le \sqrt{2 \lambda_2}
    \end{equation*}
  \end{theorem}

  \begin{conjecture}
    Extension to directed hypergraphs admits a polynomial bound in high dimensions.
  \end{conjecture}
\end{frame}
